Telecom T1}} ==History== ===The Beginning (2012)=== SK Telecom T1 made their debut at [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_VII/Cologne|IEM Cologne]] in 2012, with [[Reapered]], [[H0R0]], [[MighTiLy]], [[UandME]] and [[StarLast]] securing the title for the Korean team with a 2-1 victory against [[Fnatic]]. This team then split up into [[SK Telecom T1 K]] and [[SK Telecom T1 S]]. {{See also|T1/History|l1=History of T1}} ===SKT T1 Dynasty (2015-2017)=== The two teams were merged ahead of 2015 to form a line-up of [[MaRin]], [[Bengi]], [[T0M]], [[Faker]], [[Easyhoon]], [[Bang]], [[Wolf (Korean player)|Wolf]] and [[Piccaboo]]. This team looked like a top challenger right away, winning the [[LCK/2015/Spring|LCK 2015 Spring Split]], before placing 2nd at [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2015|MSI 2015]]. After their [[LCK/2015/Summer|LCK 2015 Summer Split]] championship, SKT won their second [[World_Championship/2015|World Championship]] (first as the merged team), beating countrymates [[KOO Tigers]] 3-1 in the finals. From here on, SK Telecom T1 won 3 titles back to back, the [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_X/World_Championship|IEM Season X World Championship]], [[LCK/2016/Spring|LCK 2016 Spring Split]] and [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2016|MSI 2016]], with [[KT Rolster]] breaking their streak by taking them out 3-2 in the [[LCK/2016/Summer|LCK 2016 Summer Semi-Finals]]. Despite this, [[World Championship/2016|Worlds 2016]] was won by SKT, making them the first team to win back-to-back titles. This performance seemed to carry on in 2017, with them winning [[LCK/2017/Spring|Spring 2017]] and [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2017|MSI 2017]], but they lost in the [[LCK/2017/Summer|LCK 2017 Summer finals]] against [[Longzhu Gaming]], with [[Samsung Galaxy]] taking away their [[World_Championship/2017|Worlds 2017]] title. ===Slumps and Struggles (2018-2021)=== {{Quote |quote=저희 SKT T1은 부진은 있어도 몰락은 없습니다.
[ Us, SKT T1, we may falter, but we never fail. ] |sign=[[kkOma]] |source=LCK Spring 2016 Finals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/AeWukfKV-y8?t=16321|title=LCK Spring Playoffs - Finals: ROX vs. SKT|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2016-04-23}} }} In [[LCK/2018/Spring|Spring 2018]], [[Untara]] and [[Blank]] joined the team as starting players. This resulted in the team placing {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} and making more changes heading into [[LCK/2018/Summer|Summer]]: [[Thal]] replaced [[Untara]], [[Pirean]] joined as secondary midlaner, while [[Effort]] replaced [[Wolf (Korean player)|Wolf]] permanently. This is when SK Telecom T1 missed out on playoffs, placing {{Ordinal|7|sup=yes}} in the regular season. It eventually resulted in them failing to qualify for [[World Championship/2018|Worlds]] too, with a 2-3 loss against [[Gen.G Esports]] in the [[LCK/2018/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]]. After the disappointing results, SK Telecom T1 rebuilt their team heading into 2019. [[Khan]] joining as a toplaner, [[Clid]] joining as a jungler, [[Teddy]] joining from [[Jin Air Green Wings]] as the new AD Carry and [[Mata]] joining the team from rivals [[KT Rolster]]. This resulted in several titles throughout the year, with them winning the [[LCK/2019/Spring|LCK 2019 Spring Split]] and [[LCK/2019/Summer|LCK 2019 Summer Split]], but coming short at the international events, exiting both in {{Ordinal|3-4|sup=yes}} place. This resulted in another rebuild heading into 2020, with [[Roach]], [[Cuzz]] and [[Effort]] joining the starting line-up. They won the [[LCK/2020/Spring|LCK 2020 Spring Split]], but placed {{Ordinal|5|sup=yes}} in [[LCK/2020/Summer|Summer]] and failed to qualify for [[World Championship/2020|Worlds 2020]] following a [[LCK/2020/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]] loss against [[Gen.G Esports]]. Trying to build on the young roster, T1 managed to sign Ryu "[[Keria]]" Min-seok who had just been released from [[DRX]], who would be replacing [[Effort]] who ended up leaving for [[SANDBOX Gaming]] later that year. This roster would place {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} in [[LCK/2021/Spring|Spring 2021]], with a lot of criticism coming T1's way for their extreme amount of player switching throughout the regular season. In [[LCK/2021/Summer|Summer 2021]], coaches [[Daeny]] and [[Zefa]] were released from the team in the middle of the split, with [[Stardust (Korean player)|Stardust]] and [[Moment]] joining as temporary coaches. They placed second in the Summer split, losing against [[DAMWON Gaming]] in the finals, but managed to secure a ticket to [[World Championship|Worlds 2021]] with a 3-2 win against [[Hanwha Life Esports]] in the [[LCK/2021/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]]. Following T1's {{Ordinal|3-4|sup=yes}} place finish at [[World Championship/2021|Worlds 2021]], the team parted ways with [[Canna]], [[Ellim]], [[Cuzz]], [[Clozer]], [[Teddy]] and [[Hoit]]. ===The Beginning of ZOFGK Roster (2022)=== T1 promoted [[Zeus]] to the starting roster, forming the [[Zeus]]-[[Oner]]-[[Faker]]-[[Gumayusi]]-[[Keria]] (ZOFGK) roster. T1 managed to become the first [[LCK]] team to ever go undefeated in the regular season, beating their own [[LCK/2015/Summer|LCK Summer 2015]] record, where they finished with a 17-1 record. After winning the [[LCK/2022/Spring|Spring 2022]] 3-1 over [[Gen.G Esports]], the team would go to [[Mid-Season Invitational/2022|MSI 2022]] making it to the knockout stage with a 7-3 record in the rumble stage qualifying second. The team would face [[G2]], a team that went 1-1 with in the rumble stage but would clean sweep them in a 3-0 series. Their next opponent was [[Royal Never Give Up]] where T1 would take blows with them and eventually would go to game 5 where T1 lost out and saw [[Royal Never Give Up]] become champions in Korea. The [[LCK/2022/Summer|Summer Split]] saw T1 end the group stage as {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} place with a 15-3 record. T1 would stop the reverse sweep of [[DAMWON Gaming]] winning the series 3-2 and once again found themselves against [[Gen.G Esports]]; this time getting swept in the finals losing 3-0. At [[World Championship/2022|Worlds 2022]] they found themselves in a group with [[EDward Gaming]], [[Cloud9]] and [[Fnatic]]. They made it out of groups as the first seed 5-1. In the quaterfinals they would face [[Royal Never Give Up]] getting their revenge T1 would sweep the LPL team winning 3-0. The next oppnent was the LPL's first seed [[JD Gaming]]. T1 would drop the first game but ultimately won 3-1. In the finals they would face [[DRX]]. T1 would take the lead 2-1 but then [[DRX]] would eventually win the series 3-2. Following T1's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} place finish they decided to keep the same ZOFGK roster for the 2023 season. ===Reignition of SKT Legacy (2023)=== In 2023, T1 had a strong start in the [[LCK/2023/Spring|LCK 2023 Spring Split]] with a 17-1 record but lost the Grand Final to [[Gen.G Esports]]. Despite this, they directly qualified for the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2023|MSI 2023]] playoffs, where they had a series of victories and defeats, eventually losing to [[Bilibili Gaming]] in the Lower Bracket Final. One month after the start of the [[LCK/2023/Summer|Summer Split]], [[Faker]] was temporarily benched due to an injury, with [[Poby]] standing in for Faker's position. Despite having a tough 1-7 record during one month of Faker's absence, and despite [[Bengi]]'s resignation as the head coach that happened mid-season, they managed to come back up and ended the regular season {{Ordinal|5|sup=yes}} with a 9-9 record. They had a series of wins in the playoffs but were swept by [[Gen.G Esports]] in the Grand Final. Still, they qualified for [[World Championship/2023|Worlds 2023]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed with the accumulated points. T1 made their way through the Swiss stage with a 3-1 record, only dropping a match against [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]]. After sweeping [[BLG]] 2-0 in their last match of Swiss Stage, they first had to face of against [[LNG Esports]] from the [[LPL]]. As they entered the last quarterfinals match, after the fall of all other LCK teams in Worlds, T1 had become the "LCK's final hope"{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/RUWVgBceVdI|title=LNG vs T1 {{!}} SCOUT VS FAKER {{!}} Quarterfinals Day 4 Tease {{!}} Worlds 2023|author=|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-05}} by being the only team remaining in Worlds outside of the LPL. T1 was were able to sweep 3-0 against LNG. {{Quote |quote=And even as every other LCK team falls away, FAKER stays standing. T1 stays standing! The last light of the LCK burns bright at Busan, as they head to the semifinals! |sign=[[Drakos]] |source=Worlds 2023 Quarterfinals Day 4{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/I8DcHjbKcII?t=2276|title=LNG vs. T1 - Game 3 {{!}} KNOCKOUTS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} LNG Esports vs T1 (2023)|publisher=LoL Esports VODs and Highlights|date=2023-11-05}} }} Their next opponent was [[JD Gaming]], a team that was looking to complete their "Golden Road" and were seen as the favourites to win the tournament. However, T1 was able to come out on top in the series with a 3-1 upset. {{Quote |quote=It is not LPL versus LCK, it is T1 versus the LPL! And they like those odds, as they move to Finals! |sign=[[Drakos]] |source=Worlds 2023 Semifinals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/yV8NwMgqcD4&t=2714|title=JDG vs. T1 - Game 4 {{!}} SEMIFINALS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} JDG Intel Esports Club vs T1 (2023)|author=|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-12}} }} With their victory, T1 entered their sixth World Finals; this time being faced with [[Weibo Gaming]]. T1 dominated the series and swept the final LPL team 3-0, becoming the first team to win 4 Worlds titles. {{Quote |quote=It was 7 years since their last, and a decade since their first; the SKT legacy has been reignited! T1 will be your 2023 WORLD CHAMPIONS! |sign=[[Atlus]] |source=Worlds 2023 Grand Final{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/LmD_ShTbIq0?t=2240|title=WBG vs. T1 - Game 3 {{!}} FINALS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} Weibo Gaming vs T1 (2023)|author=|publisher=LoL Esports VODs and Highlights|date=2023-11-19}} }} Shortly after the team's victory, contracts of players [[Gumayusi]], [[Keria]], and [[Zeus]] were renewed as they were due to expire after Worlds. The team also announced the return of [[kkOma]] as the head coach. ===The New T1 Empire (2024)=== With the same ZOFGK roster, T1 started off the year strong, by only dropping a single match against [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]] in the first round of [[LCK/2024/Spring|Spring]] regular season. At the same time, T1 started getting [[wikipedia:Denial-of-service attack#Distributed DoS|distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks]], which later affected the entire league. This resulted in extended game pauses and switching to pre-recorded streams in LCK. T1 was severely affected by the attacks, affecting their practices and their overall form.{{cite web|url=https://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=294288|title=T1 김정균 감독 "디도스 피해 심각...연습도 쉽지 않다"|trans_title=T1 Head Coach Kim Jeong-gyun "The damage from DDoS is serious... Doing practices is not easy"|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|author=김홍제|publisher=INVEN}} Although they finished second in the regular season, they were swept 0-3 by [[HLE]], with Faker admitting that not being able to practice in solo ranked affected them heavily.{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/ylzHNKBrcZo|title=0대 3 패배 T1 페이커 "다른 팀에 비해 솔로랭크 연습 못한 영향 있었다"|trans_title=T1 Faker after 0-3 loss "Not being able to practice with solo ranked compared to other teams affected us"|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|publisher=fomos esports}} Despite the challenges, T1 managed to sweep [[Dplus]] 3-0 in the lower bracket, then took revenge on [[HLE]] with a 3-1 win in the [[Match:ID LCK24SprPO R03-M002|Lower Bracket Final]], securing their spot in the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2024|MSI]]. Although T1 secured the match point first, T1 lost their Grand Final for the fourth time in a row against [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]]. ==Gallery== ===Team Photos=== SKT Worlds 2013.jpg|[[SK Telecom T1 K]] are crowned champions at [[World_Championship/2013|Worlds 2013]]
